title: Studying Topological DNA Interactions by Purified Fission Yeast Condensin
author: Tang, Uhlmann

steps.title: Streak colonies for expression screening
steps.instruction: After the third transformation, streak at least ten colonies onto a new selection plate to increase the chance of finding a suitable expression strain.

steps.title: Induce condensin expression in small cultures
steps.instruction: Grow each colony in 50 mL YPR medium at 25 °C until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.6–1.0, add 5 mL filtered 20 % galactose solution to induce, then continue shaking at 25 °C for 4 h.

steps.title: Harvest and pellet cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cultures at 4,000 × g, 4 °C for 3 min and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Lyse cells by bead beating
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold ddH₂O and transfer to a 2 mL screw‑cap cell‑breaker tube; centrifuge at 6,000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min and discard supernatant; resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL ice‑cold IgG lysis buffer, add 0.5 mL glass beads and lyse using a FastPrep‑24 (default Saccharomyces cerevisiae program); cool at 4 °C for 5 min; repeat the bead‑beating cycle two more times; confirm efficient breakage by microscopy and adjust cycles if needed; puncture the tube and collect the lysate by brief centrifugation.

steps.title: Bind condensin to IgG agarose
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL ice‑cold IgG lysis buffer to the lysate, mix, and centrifuge at 17,000 × g, 4 °C for 30 min; carefully transfer the clear supernatant to a low‑binding microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the white cloudy top layer and the pellet; add 10 µL Rabbit IgG agarose beads (20 µL bead suspension) and rotate at 4 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Wash IgG beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bead suspension at 2,000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min and discard the supernatant; resuspend beads in 1 mL IgG wash buffer, invert, centrifuge again at 2,000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min and discard; repeat the wash two additional times (total three washes).

steps.title: Analyze bound condensin by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in 20 µL SDS‑PAGE sample buffer, boil at 95 °C for 5 min, load 5 µL onto a 4 %–12 % gradient Tris‑Glycine gel, run the gel, and stain with Coomassie Blue.

steps.title: Select stoichiometric expression strain
steps.instruction: Identify the colony whose SDS‑PAGE lane shows five bands of equal intensity, indicating stoichiometric subunit composition; transfer that strain to a 15 % glycerol stock and store at –70 °C.

steps.title: Grind frozen yeast cells
steps.instruction: Freeze harvested yeast cells in liquid nitrogen and grind using a Cole‑Parmer cryogenic Freezer/Mill (6 cycles of 1 min cooling followed by 2 min grinding at 15 cps); keep tubes no more than two‑thirds full.

steps.title: Thaw powder and extract with IgG lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Thaw the yeast powder at 4 °C, mix thoroughly with 100 mL IgG lysis buffer, ensuring complete thawing and no clumps.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 100,000 × g (≈35,000 rpm in a Beckman 45Ti rotor) at 4 °C for 45 min; carefully transfer the cleared lysate to a clean 200 mL Duran bottle, avoiding the white flurry layer on top and the brown viscous layer at the bottom.

steps.title: Capture condensin on IgG agarose beads
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL Rabbit IgG‑Agarose beads (4 mL bead suspension) to the cleared lysate derived from an 8 L culture, seal and roll at 4 °C for 1 h; pour the bead slurry into a clean gravity flow column (e.g., Bio‑Rad Econo‑Pac).

steps.title: Wash beads and remove chaperones
steps.instruction: Wash the beads once with 20 mL IgG wash buffer; optionally wash a second time with 10 mL IgG wash buffer supplemented with 10 mM MgCl₂ and 1 mM ATP; then wash six additional times with 20 mL IgG wash buffer each.

steps.title: Elute condensin by on‑bead proteolysis
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in 20 mL IgG wash buffer, transfer to a 50 mL tube, add 40 µg 3C protease and 40 µg RNase A, seal and roll at 4 °C overnight (≈16 h); the next day, pour the beads onto a clean gravity column and collect the flow‑through containing eluted condensin.

steps.title: Heparin affinity chromatography
steps.instruction: Load the eluate onto a 1 mL Hi‑Trap Heparin column pre‑equilibrated with Heparin A buffer using an AKTA system; wash with 20 mL Heparin A buffer; elute with a 20 mL linear gradient from Heparin A to Heparin B, collecting 0.5 mL fractions.

steps.title: Screen fractions for nuclease contamination (optional)
steps.instruction: For each 0.5 mL fraction, incubate 10 µL with 50 ng supercoiled pBlueScript plasmid in 10 mM MgCl₂ at 30 °C for 1 h; add 0.5 % SDS and 1 µg/mL Proteinase K, incubate at 50 °C for 30 min; resolve DNA on a 0.8 % agarose gel stained with GelRed; fractions showing only supercoiled DNA are free of nuclease activity.

steps.title: Pool nuclease‑free peak fractions
steps.instruction: Combine the peak fractions that show no nuclease activity.

steps.title: Concentrate condensin by ultrafiltration
steps.instruction: Concentrate the pooled sample to 0.5 mL using a Vivaspin 6 concentrator.

steps.title: Size‑exclusion chromatography (Superose 6)
steps.instruction: Load the concentrated condensin onto a Superose 6 gel‑filtration column pre‑equilibrated with gel‑filtration buffer; collect 0.25 mL fractions.

steps.title: Finalize purified condensin
steps.instruction: Pool the peak fractions, concentrate again to approximately 1 mg/mL by ultrafiltration, aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –70 °C (stable for several months).

steps.title: Order triply digoxygenin‑labeled primers
steps.instruction: Obtain primers MT392 and MT393, each triple‑digoxygenin‑labeled, from a synthesis provider (e.g., Integrated DNA Technologies); ensure the triple labeling because singly labeled primers detach during incubations.

steps.title: First PCR amplification of template
steps.instruction: Amplify the pEGFP‑C1 plasmid (ClonTech) using primers MT462 and MT463 with CloneAmp PCR reagents according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Gel‑purify first PCR product
steps.instruction: Separate the PCR product on a 0.8 % Tris‑Acetate‑EDTA agarose gel, excise the band, and purify using the Nucleospin gel‑and‑PCR cleanup kit per the supplier’s protocol.

steps.title: Second PCR with digoxygenin primers
steps.instruction: Use the purified first‑round product as template for a second PCR with the triply digoxygenin‑labeled primers MT392 and MT393, again employing CloneAmp PCR reagents according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Gel‑purify second PCR product
steps.instruction: Run the second PCR on a 0.8 % Tris‑Acetate‑EDTA agarose gel and purify the DNA using the Nucleospin gel‑and‑PCR cleanup kit.

steps.title: Quantify dig‑DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the yield and concentration of the final digoxygenin‑labeled dsDNA using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Store dig‑DNA substrate
steps.instruction: Aliquot the purified dig‑DNA and store at –20 °C; it remains stable for up to one year.
